slides.title: A window function performs a calculation across a set of table rows that are somehow

content.name: TextBox 3
paragraphs: A window function performs a calculation across a set of table rows that are somehow

content.name: TextBox 4
paragraphs: related to the current row. This is comparable to the type of calculation that can be

content.name: TextBox 5
paragraphs: done with an aggregate function. However, window functions do not cause rows to

content.name: TextBox 6
paragraphs: become grouped into a single output row like non-window aggregate calls would.

content.name: TextBox 7
paragraphs: Instead, the rows retain their separate identities. Behind the scenes, the window

content.name: TextBox 8
paragraphs: function is able to access more than just the current row of the query result.

content.name: TextBox 5
paragraphs: (RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
• No PARTITION BY: the entire result is one partition
• No ORDER BY: all rows are peers
• With ORDER BY: default frame is RANGE UNBOUNDED PRECEDING
• Without ORDER BY: default frame includes all rows
• MySQL does not implement the EXCLUDE clause

content.name: TextBox 5
paragraphs: • PARTITION BY creates multiple independent partitions
• ORDER BY controls row order within each partition
• ROWS counts physical rows; RANGE includes peers by order key
• MySQL 8.0 has no GROUPS or EXCLUDE window-frame clause
• RANK has gaps; DENSE_RANK does not
• FIRST_VALUE / LAST_VALUE / NTH_VALUE depend on window frames
• LAG / LEAD / RANK are partition-level functions
• Several named windows may appear in a WINDOW clause
